project_requirements.title: What the call wants
project_requirements.question: What must the project address, develop and achieve?

cards.title: Central object
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop?
cards.answer: Develop and demonstrate low-voltage direct-current microgrids that can run a building’s or neighbourhood’s electrical equipment.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Scope
cards.question: Which activities fall within the funding opportunity's scope?
cards.answer: Design, demonstrate and assess a low-voltage direct-current microgrid in an urban setting. Cover flexibility, lifecycle impacts, local regulations, standards and how the system could be replicated.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Specific conditions

cards.title: Problem
cards.question: What type of problem or need must justify the project, and where must it originate?
cards.answer: Cities need to know whether local direct-current networks can avoid power conversion losses and help buildings coordinate flexible electricity use.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Deliverables
cards.question: Which concrete outputs must the project produce?
cards.answer: Deliver live and virtual demonstrations, recommendations on regulatory obstacles, use cases for standards and training materials for those who will use or install the system.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer: Show measurable energy savings and how local resources can support flexibility. Capture what the changes mean for users, including vulnerable consumers.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: After the project
cards.question: How must the result be replicated, taken up and kept in use after the project?
cards.answer: Prepare training for designers, installers and residents, and share standards use cases. Organise a workshop with site visits and collaborate with other selected projects.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Number of partners
cards.question: What is the permitted or required consortium size?
cards.answer: At least three cities from different eligible countries must participate as funded partners. At least one must be established in a European Union Member State. The other two must be established in different Member States or countries associated with Horizon Europe (countries formally participating in the European research programme). The three funded independent-organisation minimum applies as well.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · Consortium composition
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Specific conditions

cards.title: Partner composition
cards.question: Which types of partners must the consortium include?
cards.answer: Three cities from different eligible countries must participate as funded partners through their local authorities or explicitly mandated entities. At least one must be a selected European climate-neutral cities mission city. The work needs social sciences and humanities expertise.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · Consortium composition

cards.title: Distribution of work
cards.question: How must work and budget be distributed among partners?
cards.answer: Plan work and resources for cooperation with the European cities mission platform. Separate live deployment from virtual replication studies while connecting the results.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Specific conditions

cards.title: Coordinator
cards.question: What type of organisation may or must act as lead applicant?
cards.answer: The group appoints a funded partner to lead the work on urban direct-current microgrids and represent it to the funder.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · Consortium roles, Coordinator and Associated partners

project_requirements.title: TenneT's position
project_requirements.question: What is TenneT's position within the consortium?

cards.title: Coordinate
cards.question: Can TenneT apply or coordinate, and under which conditions?
cards.answer: TenneT could coordinate the project if it can contribute a defined system or standards task alongside the mandatory city participants. The applicants choose their coordinator (the funded partner that represents the group to the funder). The proposal still needs the three required city participants.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 5, 11–13 · B — Eligibility
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · Consortium roles, Coordinator and Associated partners

cards.title: Participate
cards.question: Can TenneT take part without receiving funding?
cards.answer: TenneT could take part in urban direct-current microgrids without receiving a grant. As an associated partner (an organisation that works without a grant), it could contribute a defined system or standards task alongside the mandatory city participants. It would cover its own costs and would not count towards the minimum number of funded partners. Only funded participation counts for a mandatory practitioner or city role under the topic’s rules.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 5, 11–13 · B — Eligibility

cards.title: Receive funding
cards.question: Can TenneT receive funding, and which funding rate or cost rules apply?
cards.answer: TenneT can receive up to 70% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow) for qualifying work. The Dutch entity could contribute a defined system or standards task alongside the mandatory city participants. Budget at least 30% of those costs from other resources. The rate helps set a lump sum (a fixed grant paid for accepted work rather than reimbursing actual spending).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount

cards.title: TenneT's likely contribution
cards.question: What contribution would make TenneT credible and useful within the project?
cards.answer: TenneT could assess how flexibility from local microgrids affects the transmission network. City and distribution partners would need to lead on the deployment setting and local interfaces.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Scope

project_requirements.title: Innovation
project_requirements.question: What type of innovation must the project develop?

cards.title: Innovation threshold
cards.question: Must the project produce genuinely new knowledge or technology, or may it integrate and apply existing solutions?
cards.answer: Develop innovative design methods and tools for urban microgrids. Build on prior European work on direct-current distribution, including the Shift2DC (Shift to Direct Current) project.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Scope

cards.title: Innovation object
cards.question: In what must the project innovate?
cards.answer: The innovation spans network design, use of local flexibility and safe, sustainable installation, with new regulatory and standards options.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Scope

cards.title: Development stages
cards.question: Which development stages must the project cover?
cards.answer: Design a microgrid, check local rules, run at least one live demonstration and simulate how it would work in other buildings.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Scope

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?
cards.answer: The work should reach TRL 7–8 (technology readiness level: from a prototype demonstrated in operation to a complete, qualified system) by project end.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Specific conditions

project_requirements.title: Work
project_requirements.question: Which activities or work structure must the project cover?

cards.title: Demonstration
cards.question: Where and under which conditions must the solution be demonstrated?
cards.answer: Use at least three real and virtual demonstrations in total, including a live building or neighbourhood and at least one renovation in the virtual work.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Specific conditions

cards.title: Integration
cards.question: How must the activities fit together and with existing systems?
cards.answer: Connect all electrical applications in at least one building or neighbourhood. Use simulations to check fit with other building types, including at least one renovation.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Scope

cards.title: Evidence
cards.question: What must the demonstration prove?
cards.answer: Measure energy savings and assess flexibility, lifecycle cost and social effects, including the impact on vulnerable consumers’ bills.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: User participation
cards.question: How must users take part in the project?
cards.answer: At least three cities must be funded partners, through their authority or a mandated organisation. Engage building users and the wider value chain through outreach, training and site visits.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Scope

cards.title: Safety and cybersecurity
cards.question: Which safety, cybersecurity or data requirements must the project meet?
cards.answer: Develop safe microgrid designs and address the local regulatory framework and applicable grid connection arrangements in the proposal.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Scope

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
The Commission indicates EUR 20 million for urban direct-current microgrids. It expects 3 awards.
- Grant request: around EUR 7 million per project. Different requests remain eligible.
- Funding form: Lump sum (a fixed grant paid for accepted work rather than reimbursing actual spending).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · p. 27 · Overview of this call
Innovative microgrids for improved energy system integration and efficiency in urban contexts · Budget overview

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
For-profit organisations can receive up to 70% towards urban direct-current microgrids. The rate is used to set the lump sum (a fixed grant paid for accepted work rather than reimbursing actual spending).
- For-profit organisations: Up to 70% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow), leaving at least 30% to cover.
- Non-profit legal entities: Up to 100% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–160 · Specific conditions

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
Plan the budget for urban direct-current microgrids using the cost categories allowed by the grant. Use estimates to set the fixed grant.
- Budget detail: Set out the main cost categories by beneficiary (organisations formally responsible for funded work) and work package (separately planned blocks of project work).
- Purchases and subcontracting: Apply best-value and conflict-of-interest rules.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents
Lump Sum Funding in Horizon Europe: What do I need to know? · pp. 6–7, 26–27 · Detailed budget table

cards.title: Cash flow and financial exposure
cards.answer:
Plan cash flow for urban direct-current microgrids around acceptance of completed blocks of work.
- Payment model: Pre-financing (an advance at the start of the grant), then periodic payments for accepted work packages (separately planned blocks of project work) and a final balance.
- Retention or guarantee: 5–8% of the maximum grant is deducted from pre-financing for mutual insurance.
- Financial reporting or audit: Keep evidence of implementation and completion.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 33 · Reporting & payment arrangements
Lump Sum Funding in Horizon Europe: What do I need to know? · pp. 17–23 · Payment schedule, Reporting and payment, Keeping records

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
Apply for urban direct-current microgrids through the European Funding & Tenders Portal in one stage.
- Full proposal: 7 October 2027 at 17:00 Brussels time. The technical proposal (Part B) is limited to 45 pages.
- Opening: 9 February 2027.

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
The grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules) sets the start date and duration for urban direct-current microgrids.
- Required start: Work normally starts after the grant agreement is signed. A reasoned exception needs approval.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 30–31 · Starting date & project duration

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
The Commission’s timetable for assessing and contracting urban direct-current microgrids is indicative.
- Expected invitation or assessment result: Around 5 months from the full-proposal deadline.
- Grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules): Around 8 months from the full-proposal deadline.
- Conditions before starting: Beneficiaries (organisations formally responsible for funded work) must conclude a written consortium agreement (the partners’ written agreement on how the project will run).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 30 · Indicative timetable for evaluation and for signature of the grant agreement

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
Use the portal’s forms to submit the proposal and supporting documents for urban direct-current microgrids.
- Application form: Complete Part A in the Portal and attach Part B and mandatory annexes.
- Registration: Beneficiaries (organisations formally responsible for funded work) and affiliated entities (organisations legally linked to funded partners) need participant identification codes (organisation registration numbers).
- Partner documents: The coordinator confirms its authority to act for the applicant group.
- Budget: Provide the detailed lump-sum (a fixed grant paid for accepted work rather than reimbursing actual spending) budget table with the full proposal.
- Mandatory application input: Include an explicit authority to act for the applicant group statement if a participating entity represents a city. Retained proposals need a formal signed and dated authority to act for the applicant group letter during grant preparation.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Urban direct-current microgrids proposals compete on research quality, impact and the quality of the delivery plan.
- Full proposal: Excellence, impact and implementation are scored. Each criterion needs 3/5 and the total needs 10/15.
- Impact is weighted by 1.5 in Innovation Action (a grant for developing and demonstrating new solutions) full-proposal ranking.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 23–26 · D — Award criteria

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
The urban microgrid proposal needs cities that meet the topic’s specific eligibility rules.
- Conditional requirement: Document readiness for real-life deployment with a review of local regulation and grid codes and evidence that the installations can proceed.
- Conditional requirement: Resource collaboration with the Cities Mission Platform and conclude the memorandum of understanding as soon as possible after the project starts.
- Conditional requirement: Screen partners for China-control restrictions.
